answer: A reef survives because every polyp filters what passes through it, and an agent economy can do the same at its bridge: a newcomer crosses only after two unrelated established agents independently verify one real piece of its work, and each failed crossing burns a small non-refundable fee that doubles next time. A violet flag marks identities whose funders cluster together, freezing their weight until a fresh, unrelated sponsor vouches with locked stake. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a whole reef of independent verifiers is not.
